source_notes.note: Registered source is arXiv2103.06476v9 marked14Mar2024,69pages. Actual main text ends on28 before References y638.557, clipped632. The outline has stale/displaced labels and page references; actual bold headings establish exactly six Theorems. Proposition2.5 and Corollary2.6 are not added as Theorems. Appendix bodies begin33 and remain excluded.

Definition2.1 is almost-sure relative-width approximation to an existing valid CS with the same center. Definition2.7 instead describes limiting all-future coverage as the starting index m increases. Neither definition is substituted for the other; T2.8 additionally proves an ordinary limit equality. Separate marginal-in-time coverage is insufficient.

Definition2.1 requires strictly positive bounds at every time. T2.2 assumes finite variance without explicitly excluding zero population variance, and its empirical variance is zero at t=1. Rho_m also divides by the variance estimate at m. No initial padding, start-time or degenerate-case convention is printed in these statements; preserve and flag rather than silently correcting them.

The numerator -2log(alpha)+log(-2log(alpha))+1 in rho_m can be negative for alpha sufficiently close to1, while the source generally allows alpha∈(0,1). A further domain restriction would be required for that displayed square root to be real. Rho_m also depends on estimated variance at the first peeking time, so it must not be replaced by arbitrary fixed rho in the sharp-coverage theorem.

The prose before L1 says the average variance either does not vanish or does so superlinearly. Formal L1 requires V_t=t times average variance to diverge; surrounding explanation says the average does not vanish faster than1/t, with an omega_a.s.(1/t) formula. Preserve the original wording and use the explicit formal condition, without rewriting it.

The source globally suppresses a.s. on little-o/big-O. Later nuisance convergence, product rates and uniform/average conditions inherit almost-sure meaning. Do not downgrade them to in-probability rates because L2(P) norms themselves resemble mean-square convergence.

T3.1 explicitly bounds the true propensity away from0 and1, and T3.2 inherits this common setup while estimating propensity. The main-text statements do not separately bound or clip estimated propensities, though they enter denominators. T3.3 does not explicitly import T3.1 overlap; retain named causal positivity and its own moment hypotheses without inventing a stronger uniform-overlap premise.

Consistency, positivity and exchangeability are named and cited rather than formally expanded in the main text. Mu^a is described as a conditional mean function and used in the identified ATE/EIF formulas, but a separate explicit conditional-regression equality is not printed in these passages. Preserve this source limitation instead of synthesizing an original definition or reading an appendix.

Formula24 is explicitly an uncentered EIF; subtracting psi would change the AIPW estimator25. Formula27 uses potentially misspecified regression limits with the true propensity. T3.1 allows such limits, whereas T3.2 requires consistent nuisance functions and convergence to the efficient f. Its common-setup reference does not reimpose known propensity.

The infinity-subscript split streams are counted at current time t by an explicit convention. Early times may leave a fold empty; the source does not define all estimator/variance values then. Variance26 averages two fold variances equally, not by random fold size, and the within-fold normalization is named sample variance rather than reprinted. Preserve these choices and ambiguities.

T3.3 prints varhat_t(bar-f), not varhat_t(hat-f). The former is not separately defined in the main text as an observable statistic; Corollary2.6 uses sample variance while26 defines a cross-fit fitted variance. Preserve the printed expression and unresolved interpretation. No fabricated equivalence or direct D22 dependency is introduced for T3.3.

Section3.4 permits changing data distributions and expected treatment effects but writes common functions mu^a andpi without time subscripts. Their applicability across all t is not fully spelled out beyond the displayed conditions. The term individual treatment effects denotes expected Y_t^1-Y_t^0 in the source, not realized unit-level effects. Uniformity over all i in ATE1 differs from the average-product condition ATE2.

T3.3 imports all Corollary2.6 assumptions after substituting bar-f(Z_t): L1, positive-delta Lyapunov summability, squared-observation moments, mean growth and relative mean variation. The following informal statement that pointwise-in-i product rates imply the averaged ATE2 rate needs uniform control and is not used as a replacement for the actual average condition.

The abstract theorem permits general totally ordered infinite time sets. Meaning of t→infinity, existence of a cofinal sequence and simultaneous-event measurability require ordinary analytical conventions not fully specified for arbitrary ordered sets. Preserve the source generality. Hatted approximating boundaries, unadorned approximate widths and starred valid widths are distinct objects.
